definitions.gloss: incense; fragrant substance burned for its scent
definitions.explanation: Aromatic materials, typically in stick or cone form, burned to produce pleasant fragrance. Used in religious ceremonies, meditation, and as home fragrance.

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}る{前|まえ}にお{香|こう}を{焚|た}くとよく{眠|ねむ}れる。
examples.english: Burning incense before bed helps me sleep well.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{毎朝|まいあさ}{仏壇|ぶつだん}の{前|まえ}でお{香|こう}を{焚|た}いている。
examples.english: My grandmother burns incense in front of the Buddhist altar every morning.

notes:
The polite prefix お is standard for this word; plain {香|こう} is used in compounds but rarely alone in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{香|こう}を{焚|た}く: to burn incense
- お{香|こう}を{供|そな}える: to offer incense
- お{香|こう}の{香|かお}り: the scent of incense
- {線香|せんこう}: stick incense

CULTURAL NOTE:
Incense has deep roots in Japanese culture, used in Buddhist ceremonies, tea ceremony, and the traditional art of {香道|こうどう} (the Way of Incense). Modern use includes aromatherapy and home fragrance. Common types include {白檀|びゃくだん} (sandalwood) and {沈香|じんこう} (agarwood).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {線香|せんこう}: stick incense — specifically the thin sticks used at altars and graves
- {香料|こうりょう}: fragrance materials — broader term including perfumery ingredients
- アロマ: aroma — modern loanword for aromatherapy-style fragrance
